summary.headline: Titan's Q2 FY27 jewellery margin normalised to 11.1% (11.7% ex-MTM), with ₹490 crore customs duty gain and ₹671 crore Damas liability write-back flattering reported numbers.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter with healthy growth across most brands, though macro conditions were volatile. Titan Jewellery's normalised margin was 11.1% after stripping a ₹490 crore customs duty gain (CaratLane ₹46 crore), and 11.7% after also adjusting for a roughly 60 bps MTM reversal. A new P&L line shows a ₹671 crore fair-value gain on the second Damas acquisition tranche liability, reassessed from ₹1,668 crore. Competitive intensity, gold price deflation and a festive-season timing shift weighed on jewellery buyer growth, with coins and investment buying notably soft. Management anchored FY27 jewellery margin guidance at around 11%.

segments.name: Titan Jewellery (Tanishq, Mia, Zoya)
segments.commentary: Normalised margin 11.1%, or 11.7% ex-MTM, with management citing gold price realisation pressure from grey-channel and discounted domestic gold after the customs duty hike. Studded jewellery has grown for three consecutive quarters.

segments.name: CaratLane
segments.commentary: EBIT margin fell to 6.5% from 10.2% in the base period, due to brand investment, talent spend and elevated promotions. Management still targets a gradual rise from about 8% to 9% EBIT margin.

segments.name: Watches (Titan Watches)
segments.commentary: Margins were strong, led by Edge and sales in the ₹25,000+ price points. October growth was better than Q2, with ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh a share-gain area.

segments.name: EyeCare, fragrances, fashion accessories, Taneira, TEAL, North America jewellery
segments.commentary: Management called these non-jewellery and newer businesses strong this quarter, with Taneira showing early green shoots. No quantified figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Jewellery EBIT margin anchored around 11% for FY27; no change in stance, with a full review of margin after FY27 closes.
Management expects 40-60 bps quarter-on-quarter MTM swings to recur as part of the P&L.
Buyer growth is the top priority, with volume-led growth expected if gold price cushion to ticket size fades.
Management said a healthy buyer growth figure (some quarters of 8-10%) could support 20%-plus growth, with a stated 'healthy double-digit' business growth target.
Board approved a ₹2,500 crore capital raise, which management described as a replenishment of existing borrowings rather than new debt.
capex_capacity: Diamond Expertise Centres now at 250+ stores, with benefits expected to play out over time.
Network expansion continues through new stores in existing cities and new cities across brands, plus upgrades to larger stores.
Gold exchange programme has run for about one year and is cited as a meaningful lever.
18-carat gold for core jewellery, 14-carat for Tanishq studded, and 9-carat in Mia is building catalogue depth, with adoption at pace across stores over 9-10 months.
demand_pricing: Festive pattern: a strong start from Navratri (Oct 11-22), a soft patch after Vijayadashami tied to gold rate volatility, then a recovery from the last weekend of October into Dhanteras.
Studded jewellery demand has grown across three quarters and is industry-wide, with a secular shift toward natural diamonds since January 2026. Buyer growth is higher in studded.
Coins and investment buying softened from August-September and remained soft during festive; management cited WGC data showing a significant industry drop in coins and bars.

Q2 buyer growth at TMZ was flat versus 5% in Q1, attributed to the festive shift and coins/investment softness. Plain gold jewellery growth was softer, with core jewellery a few percentage points better ex-coins.

Management sees competitive intensity rising: organised players expanding into new geographies, smaller jewellers discounting, and grey-channel gold at a discount. Gold price realisation is under pressure in the domestic market since the customs duty increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CaratLane margin fall to 6.5% from 10.2%, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a conscious choice to invest in brand building and talent, plus elevated promotions in the quarter. It still expects EBIT margin to rise from 8% to 9% over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Damas liability write-back reverse, and is it an impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said it is an accounting requirement driven by a four-year probable-performance view, reassessed quarterly. Management does not see any reduction in Damas' long-term opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Can jewellery margins rise above 11% given the mix shift away from coins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the margin anchor at around 11% for FY27, citing growth priorities, competitive response and gold price uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tanishq reverse light-weighting and lower-carat initiatives as gold prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management described 18-carat and lighter pieces as a long-term accessibility strategy, and said 22-carat remains available as an add-on choice.

qa_highlights.question: What drives watch margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge launches and Made in India campaign lifted price points, and sales at ₹25,000 and above were strong. Management hopes it will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the studded growth industry-wide or driven by Diamond Expertise Centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is industry-wide, driven by a shift toward natural diamonds and younger buyers, with DECs expected to add benefit over time.

risks_watch: Gold price deflation and the discount of domestic gold versus international prices, which could erode the customs duty benefit and pressure realisations.
Competitive intensity: smaller jewellers discounting with pre-duty inventory, grey-channel gold, and organised players expanding into new geographies.
Buyer growth at TMZ turned flat in Q2 and the October base is not like-to-like after the festive shift, making Q3 and Q4 read-through difficult.
CaratLane margin fell to 6.5% and its path back to 8-9% depends on promotion and talent spend.
Damas liability is reassessed every quarter, so further fair-value gains or losses could move reported profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth story and studded momentum, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on near-term buyer growth, October trends and ticket size. Management was evasive on specifics for October and bill values, and defensive on margin and competition.
key_quotes: We would not, as far as FY27 is concerned, change our stance on margins.
Our number one priority is to drive buyer growth, and everything we are doing is to drive buyer growth.
Competitive intensity, please expect it to continue to improve and increase all the time.

growth.why: Management says a healthy buyer growth of 8-10% could support 20%-plus growth and a 'healthy double-digit' business growth target, with network expansion and Diamond Expertise Centres (250+ stores) as support, but no numeric capacity or order backing was quantified; jewellery margin is anchored around 11% for FY27 with buyer growth flat at TMZ in Q2 versus 5% in Q1.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Jewellery EBIT margin anchored around 11% for FY27 (11.1% normalised, 11.7% ex-MTM in Q2), with gold price realisation pressure and rising competition; CaratLane margin fell to 6.5% from 10.2%, with only a gradual climb to 8-9% over a couple of years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network expansion via new stores in existing and new cities plus larger-store upgrades is planned, with no store count given; Diamond Expertise Centres already at 250+ stores, so new capacity is incremental and unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says 8-10% buyer growth could support 20%-plus growth, but TMZ buyer growth was flat in Q2 versus 5% in Q1 and October trends were not disclosed, so volume recovery is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the FY27 jewellery margin anchor at around 11% and was non-committal on near-term buyer growth, so no upward revision is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rising competition, gold price deflation eroding realisations, flat TMZ buyer growth in Q2, and quarterly Damas fair-value and MTM swings of 40-60 bps could pressure reported numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Studded and 14-carat/9-carat catalogue depth is building and Edge watch launches lifted price points, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Gold price realisation pressure and studded mix shift
rows.why: Grey-channel and discounted domestic gold after the customs duty hike pressure realisations, while studded jewellery has grown for three consecutive quarters and is driving mix.

rows.label: Damas second-tranche liability reassessment
rows.why: Liability reassessed from ₹1,668 crore after a ₹671 crore fair-value gain, and further quarterly gains or losses could move reported profit.

rows.label: CaratLane margin recovery to 8-9%
rows.why: EBIT margin fell to 6.5% from 10.2% on brand, talent and promotion spend, and recovery to 8-9% is only a gradual target.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term studded and growth story but cautious and non-committal on near-term buyer growth and October trends, and defensive on margin and competition; analysts pressed on the Damas write-back, CaratLane margin drop and whether jewellery margins can exceed 11%.
